result:
Compiles successfully. I wrote `tests/com/google/gson/internal/ConstructorConstructorAgentTest.java` (JUnit 3.8 style, extends `junit.framework.TestCase`), covering:

- `get()` returns a non-null `ObjectConstructor` and `construct()` yields a correctly-typed, independent instance each call
- exact-type `InstanceCreator` registration is honored (identity check) and receives the correct `Type`
- an `InstanceCreator` registered for an unrelated type is not triggered by other requests
- construction succeeds for a class with only a private no-arg constructor (contract says "a requested type", not "public types only")
- interface types (`List`, `Map`, `Set`) produce assignable default instances, asserted only via `instanceof` to avoid depending on unspecified concrete implementation classes
- boundary case: `get(null)` must fail with an unchecked exception, since the method declares none and cannot resolve a null type description
- `toString()` is non-null and stable across calls

`./compile.sh` reports success.
